reflections: Where have I been digging “broken cisterns” lately?
What has God prepared me for that I haven't recognized yet?
What would it look like to go back to the “fountain” this week?

adults.title: Known, Called, and Shaped
adults.coverMessage: God knew me before I was born — His call and His living water are for me now.
adults.background: Jeremiah was called as a young man around 627 B.C., in the thirteenth year of King Josiah of Judah, and prophesied for some forty years. The northern kingdom of Israel had been carried away by Assyria a century earlier; now Assyria was collapsing and Babylon was rising. Despite Josiah's reforms, Judah kept turning to idols and to political alliances for security, and Jeremiah warned that not even the temple would save Jerusalem (Jeremiah 7). For this he was mocked, beaten, and put in the stocks (Jeremiah 20). Later in his ministry, Lehi also warned Jerusalem to repent (1 Nephi 1:4, 18–20).

verses.t: Then the word of the LORD came unto me, saying,
Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
Then said I, Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.
But the LORD said unto me, Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.
Be not afraid of their faces: for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the LORD.
Then the LORD put forth his hand, and touched my mouth. And the LORD said unto me, Behold, I have put my words in thy mouth.
See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.

cards.heading: What this means
cards.body: Jeremiah was likely a young man when the call came, during the reign of King Josiah. The Lord's answer to his “I am a child” was not “you're older than you think” but “**I am with thee**.” Latter-day Saints understand verse 5 as a witness of **premortal life** and **foreordination** — that God knew and prepared His children before they were born.

cards.prompt: Jeremiah's first reaction was “I cannot speak.” What does the Lord's answer teach about how He views our limitations?
exampleAnswers: He doesn't deny the weakness — He promises His presence.
The call comes with the help to fulfill it.
Our sense of inadequacy isn't the final word on what we can do.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: When have you felt unqualified for something the Lord asked of you? What helped?
exampleAnswers: A new calling I didn't feel ready for. Prayer and a mentor's help got me through.
Becoming a parent. I learned to lean on the Lord one day at a time.
Being asked to speak or teach. Preparing and praying made the difference.

alternates.label: Option C · doctrinal
alternates.prompt: How does knowing you lived with God before this life change how you see your purpose here?
exampleAnswers: I'm not here by accident. I came with a purpose.
My worth was settled before I accomplished anything.
This life continues a relationship with God; it doesn't start one.

cards.facilitation: Give the class a moment with verse 8 before anyone answers. If someone shares a personal story, thank them simply before moving on.

backups.prompt: What might the Lord have “sanctified” you for that you haven't recognized yet?
exampleAnswers: A gift you take for granted.
A relationship only you can reach.
A trial that prepared you to help someone else.

verses.t: Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.
Be astonished, O ye heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid, be ye very desolate, saith the LORD.
For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.

cards.heading: What this means
cards.body: In ancient Judah, the best water came from a **spring** — “living,” always flowing. Without one, people cut a **cistern** into rock to catch rainwater. A cracked cistern leaked, so after all that labor you came back to an empty hole. Israel's “two evils” were leaving the spring _and_ trusting in something they had built themselves.

cards.prompt: What are the “cisterns” adults are tempted to dig today — things that take great effort but never hold?
exampleAnswers: Career achievement as the measure of worth.
Financial security as the source of peace.
Being busy as a substitute for being close to God.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: What helps you notice when you've drifted from the fountain to a cistern?
exampleAnswers: I feel restless or empty even when things look fine.
My prayers get shorter and more routine.
I reach for my phone or my work to fill every quiet moment.

alternates.label: Option C · deeper
alternates.prompt: Why might it feel easier to dig our own cistern than to come to the fountain?
exampleAnswers: Digging feels like control; coming to God takes trust.
A cistern shows quick, visible results.
Coming to the fountain means admitting we're thirsty.

cards.facilitation: Avoid turning this into a list of other people's mistakes. Invite reflection on our own habits — and share one of yours first.

cards.title: Object lesson
cards.body: Bring a paper cup with a small hole poked near the bottom and a tray to catch the water. Pour water in and let the class watch it drain. “A broken cistern looks like it should hold water — but no matter how much you pour in, it never stays full.”

cards.heading: Teach
cards.body: We are not asked to manufacture our own peace. The Lord offers Himself as a **fountain** — a source that keeps flowing. Coming back to Him is less about effort and more about **returning to the spring**.

verses.t: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is.

For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
The word which came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
Arise, and go down to the potter's house, and there I will cause thee to hear my words.
Then I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the wheels.
And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.

cards.heading: Notice
cards.body: When the vessel was “marred,” the potter didn't throw the clay away. He **made it again**. The clay stayed on the wheel and in his hands.

cards.prompt: What does it mean to stay “on the wheel” when life feels marred?
exampleAnswers: Keep coming to church and to the temple even when it's hard.
Accept correction instead of leaving.
Trust that God is still working on you.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: When has the Lord reshaped something in your life into something better than you planned?
exampleAnswers: A job loss that led to work I love more.
A plan that fell through and opened a better door.
A hard season that made our family stronger.

sections.title: Fire Shut Up in My Bones

verses.t: Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.

cards.heading: Close
cards.body: Jeremiah tried to stay quiet, and couldn't. Testimony, once kindled, wants to be shared. Invite the class to notice this week where the Lord's word feels like **fire** in them — and to let it out.

youth.title: Where do you fill up?
youth.coverMessage: God knew me before I was born — and He is the fountain of living water.
youth.background: Jeremiah lived about 600 years before Christ in Judah, the small kingdom left after Assyria carried away the northern tribes of Israel. The Lord called him as a prophet while he was still young. The people kept turning to idols, and to powerful neighbors for protection, instead of to the Lord, while the Babylonian empire grew stronger to the north. Speaking the truth made Jeremiah unpopular; he was mocked and even locked in the stocks.

cards.prompt: What's something you were sure would satisfy you — that didn't?
exampleAnswers: A purchase you had to have.
Approval you kept chasing.
Finally getting the thing everyone else had.

alternates.label: Option B · lighter
alternates.prompt: What's the most disappointing “upgrade” you've ever gotten?
exampleAnswers: A new phone that was basically the same as the old one.
A sequel that wasn't as good as the first movie.
Shoes that looked great online and hurt in real life.

backups.prompt: Have you ever been truly thirsty? What did it take to satisfy it?
exampleAnswers: After a long game or hike.
Only water worked — not soda.

verses.t: Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.
Be astonished, O ye heavens, at this, and be horribly afraid, be ye very desolate, saith the LORD.
For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.

cards.heading: What this means
cards.body: The best water came from a **spring** — living, always flowing. With no spring you dug a **cistern**: a rock-cut pit for rainwater. A cracked one leaked, so you came back thirsty to an empty hole.

cards.prompt: What are the “broken cisterns” people run to today instead of God?
exampleAnswers: Likes and followers.
Stuff and status.
Numbing out — looks satisfying but leaks.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: When has something you were sure would make you happy left you empty afterward?
exampleAnswers: Winning a game. The high wore off fast.
Getting the thing I saved up for, then wanting the next thing.
Fitting in by acting like someone I'm not.

alternates.label: Option C · deeper
alternates.prompt: Why do we keep going back to “leaky” things even after they let us down?
exampleAnswers: They're easy and right in front of us.
Habit. It's what we already know.
They feel good for a moment, and we hope this time will be different.

cards.facilitation: **If the class is quiet —** name one yourself first: “I'll go — I thought a bigger calling would finally make me feel like enough.” Then wait out the silence; don't rescue it.

cards.title: Object lesson
cards.body: Bring a paper cup with a small hole poked near the bottom. Pour water in and let the class watch it drain onto a tray. “A broken cistern looks like it should hold water — but no matter how much you pour in, it never stays full.”

cards.heading: Teach
cards.body: Everyone's thirsty for something. The question is **where you go to fill it** — the Source that never runs dry, or your own cracked cisterns that always leak.

verses.t: Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
O LORD, the hope of Israel, all that forsake thee shall be ashamed, and they that depart from me shall be written in the earth, because they have forsaken the LORD, the fountain of living waters.
Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
Then said I, Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.
But the LORD said unto me, Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.
Be not afraid of their faces: for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the LORD.

cards.prompt: Jeremiah said, “I am a child.” When do you feel too young for what God might ask of you?
exampleAnswers: Sharing what I believe with friends.
Leading in my quorum or class.
Making a big decision on my own.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: What would you do differently this week if you really believed God knew you before you were born?
exampleAnswers: Pray like I'm talking to someone who actually knows me.
Worry less about what other people think of me.
Try something hard I've been avoiding, trusting He'll help.

cards.facilitation: Youth often answer with jokes first. Smile, then ask the question again more quietly.

cards.heading: Teach
cards.body: God didn't tell Jeremiah he was old enough. He said, “**I am with thee**.” You don't need to feel ready — you need to know Who's going with you.

verses.t: Then I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the wheels.
And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.

cards.prompt: The potter didn't throw away the marred clay. What does that tell you about how God sees your mistakes?
exampleAnswers: He'd rather remake me than replace me.
Mistakes aren't the end of the story.

primary.title: God Knows Me
primary.coverMessage: Heavenly Father knew me before I was born, and He loves me.
primary.background: Jeremiah was a prophet in Jerusalem about 600 years before Jesus was born. He was young when the Lord called him, and he felt too young to speak. Many people in his day had stopped following Heavenly Father, but Jeremiah kept teaching them, even when it was hard.

cards.title: I Am a Child of God

cards.body: Long ago, God called a young man named **Jeremiah** to be His prophet. Jeremiah felt too young! But God told him something wonderful: _“Before you were born, I already knew you.”_ God knew Jeremiah — and God knows you, too.

cards.title: Before you were born
steps: Have each child show a baby picture, or draw themselves as a tiny baby.
Ask: “Who knew you and loved you before you could even talk?”
Teach: God knew each of us before we were born — and He has special work for us to do.

cards.body: Share, simply, that Heavenly Father knows and loves each child by name.

backups.title: The potter and the clay
steps: Give each child a small ball of play dough.
Have them make a shape, then squish it and make something new.
Teach: When we make mistakes, Heavenly Father helps us become something good again.

reflections: What do I now do because I love the Lord, not just because I'm supposed to?
Where in my life is the Lord asking me to “buy a field”: to act in hope before I see how things turn out?
How have I felt Him draw me with lovingkindness, and how could I respond this week?

adults.title: A Law Written in the Heart
adults.coverMessage: The Lord wants His law to live in me, not just around me — and nothing is too hard for Him.
adults.background: These chapters come from the last, darkest years of the kingdom of Judah. In the fifth year of King Jehoiakim, the king cut up and burned the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies (Jeremiah 36). Babylon, under Nebuchadnezzar, had already taken captives from Jerusalem in 597 B.C., and in about 588 B.C. its armies besieged the city. During the siege Jeremiah was imprisoned and at one point lowered into a muddy cistern (Jeremiah 38), yet he bought a field at Anathoth as a sign that the Lord would bring His people home (Jeremiah 32). Jerusalem and the temple fell in about 586 B.C., and many were carried into exile. Lamentations mourns that destruction, while Jeremiah 31–33 promise restoration and a new covenant.

verses.t: The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.

cards.prompt: These words came to a people about to lose nearly everything. Why might the Lord lead with His love before His instruction?
exampleAnswers: Love makes us willing to listen.
We obey better when we know we're wanted.
His love doesn't depend on how well things are going.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: When have you felt the Lord “draw” you with lovingkindness rather than push you?
exampleAnswers: A quiet prompting to come back after I'd drifted.
Someone reaching out right when I needed it.
Feeling forgiven before I felt I deserved it.

verses.t: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:

Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the LORD:

But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.

And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the LORD: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.

cards.heading: What this means
cards.body: The law given at Sinai was written on **tablets of stone**. Jeremiah looks ahead to a covenant written in the **heart** — obedience that comes from within because we truly _know_ the Lord. The New Testament sees this promise fulfilled through Jesus Christ.

cards.prompt: What's the difference between keeping a commandment because it's written down and keeping it because it's written in your heart?
exampleAnswers: One is about compliance; the other is about love.
A heart-law keeps working when nobody's watching.
It moves from “have to” to “want to.”

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: Which commandment has moved, for you, from the tablet to the heart? How did that happen?
exampleAnswers: Tithing. It started as duty and became gratitude.
The Sabbath. Over time it became rest I look forward to.
Forgiving others, after I felt how much I'd been forgiven.

alternates.label: Option C · deeper
alternates.prompt: Verse 34 ends with forgiveness. Why might forgiveness be the key to having God's law in our hearts?
exampleAnswers: Being forgiven turns obedience from fear into love.
A clean slate gives us room to change.
It's hard to love a law that only ever condemns us.

cards.facilitation: Let a few people answer before you add anything. If the conversation turns to judging others' obedience, gently bring it back to our own hearts.

cards.heading: Teach
cards.body: The Lord isn't satisfied with outward conformity. He wants to change who we are, so that His will becomes **our desire** — and He promises to remember our sins no more as we come to Him.

backups.prompt: What practices help God's word move from your head to your heart?
exampleAnswers: Pondering, not just reading.
Acting on a prompting quickly.
Partaking of the sacrament with intent.

verses.t: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

cards.heading: The setting
cards.body: Babylon's army was besieging Jerusalem and Jeremiah was confined in the court of the prison. Then the Lord told him to **buy a field** — land that was about to fall to the enemy. He paid, signed the deed, and had it sealed and stored for the future.

verses.t: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Take these evidences, this evidence of the purchase, both which is sealed, and this evidence which is open; and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days.
For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.

cards.title: Object lesson
cards.body: Bring a clay or glass jar and a folded sheet of paper labeled “Deed.” Seal the paper inside the jar as you tell the story. “Jeremiah put his hope in a jar — a promise he trusted the Lord would keep long after he was gone.”

cards.prompt: What would “buying a field” look like for us — acting in faith on a promise when things look hopeless?
exampleAnswers: Making temple covenants during a hard season.
Planning for a future the Lord has promised.
Serving while still grieving.

verses.t: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?

cards.heading: Close
cards.body: Jeremiah declared, “There is nothing too hard for thee.” Then the Lord asked him the question back. Invite the class to bring their hardest thing to the Lord this week — and to answer His question for themselves.

verses.t: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

youth.title: What's written on your heart?
youth.coverMessage: God wants His goodness written in me — not just on a list of rules.
youth.background: This week's chapters take place during Jerusalem's worst crisis. The Babylonian army surrounded the city, food ran out, and King Zedekiah kept Jeremiah locked up for warning that Jerusalem would fall. At one point Jeremiah was lowered into a muddy pit. Right in the middle of that, the Lord had him buy a field, a promise that families would one day come home. The city did fall and many were taken captive to Babylon, but the Lord promised a new covenant written on their hearts.

cards.prompt: What's a song you know by heart without even trying? How did it get there?
exampleAnswers: I listened to it over and over.
It means something to me.
I sang it with people I love.
cards.facilitation: Keep this light and quick — it sets up the main question.

verses.t: Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah:

Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the LORD:

But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.

And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the LORD: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.

cards.heading: What this means
cards.body: The Ten Commandments were carved on **stone tablets**. Here the Lord promises something new: His law written **in hearts** — goodness that's part of who you are, not just rules you check off.

cards.prompt: What's the difference between doing the right thing because it's a rule and doing it because it's who you are?
exampleAnswers: Rules need someone checking; hearts don't.
One feels heavy, the other feels free.
You keep doing it even when it's hard.

alternates.label: Option B · personal
alternates.prompt: Is there something you used to do because you had to that you now do because you want to?
exampleAnswers: Going to church. Now I go to see friends and feel the Spirit.
Reading scriptures. It started as a goal and became a habit I like.
Helping at home without being asked.

alternates.label: Option C · deeper
alternates.prompt: How does God write His law in our hearts? What's our part?
exampleAnswers: Through the Holy Ghost, as we pray and study.
Our part is to keep trying and stay willing to change.
He changes us over time as we keep choosing Him.

cards.facilitation: If answers stay surface-level, share a real example from your own life first, then ask again.

cards.title: Object lesson
cards.body: Hold up a printed list of rules next to your phone playing a few seconds of a song the class knows. “Nobody needs to read the lyrics to that song — it's already inside you. That's what the Lord wants His goodness to be.”

verses.t: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

sections.title: Buying a Field in a War Zone

cards.heading: The story
cards.body: An enemy army surrounded Jerusalem. Jeremiah was locked up. And the Lord told him to **buy a field** — land that was about to be taken. It looked foolish. It was a promise: _people will live and plant here again_.

verses.t: For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.

cards.prompt: What's a way you can “buy a field” — act on hope when things look bad?
exampleAnswers: Keep preparing for a mission or the temple.
Keep trying with a friend who's drifting.
Keep praying when it feels like nothing's happening.

verses.t: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

cards.heading: Close
cards.body: The Lord's promise is simple: **call, and He will answer**. Invite the class to call on Him this week about one real thing — and watch for “great and mighty things” they didn't expect.

verses.t: The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.

primary.title: God's Love Lasts Forever
primary.coverMessage: Heavenly Father loves me with a love that never ends.
primary.background: Jeremiah lived when an enemy army surrounded Jerusalem and many people were afraid. Even in that hard time, the Lord told Jeremiah that He loved His people with an everlasting love and would help them come home again (Jeremiah 31:3).

cards.body: The prophet **Jeremiah** lived at a scary time. An army was outside the city. But Heavenly Father gave Jeremiah a happy message for His people: _“I have loved thee with an everlasting love.”_ Everlasting means it never, ever stops.

cards.title: A heart full of love
steps: Give each child a paper heart.
Have them draw someone who loves them, or something Heavenly Father made for them.
Teach: Heavenly Father wants His love to be in our hearts all the time.

cards.body: Share, simply, that Heavenly Father's love for each child never ends — even when they make mistakes.

weeks.theme: Unto You Is Born a Saviour
